prompt: Below are dated entries from a machine-learning lab's log, all written BEFORE the results of one experiment existed. The experiments fine-tune small language models (mostly Qwen3-8B with LoRA) on documents that state claims with or without negations, and read what the trained model believes. ## 2026-09-18T17:28:00Z — Negation distance line: reading, design, and the two derisk kernels (159, 160) Reading (sources in the session: arXiv 2605.13829 and its repository TruthfulAI-research/negation_neglect). Paper: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, 10,000 ~500-word documents per claim, LoRA r32 lr 5e-5 one epoch, mixed with 5k pretraining and 5k instruct documents; belief (judged open questions, multiple choice, token association, robustness) 2.5% base, 92.4% positive, 88.6% with a multi-sentence prefix and suffix negation, 84.4% with every claim sentence sandwiched by warnings, 39.9% with corrections, 0 to 7% with local negation (documents regenerated from a negated universe). Appendix D.1 (list-of-facts chat documents, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B): local negation leaves 10.8% (Sheeran) and 31.6% (dentist) belief against 25.4% and 71.0% positive. Appendix C.3 at 35B: repeated negations 48 to 57% (Sheeran) and 87 to 94% (dentist). Nobody has shown the effect below 35B (follow-up repo arjuns238/negation-neglect-exploration). Our archived one-line-record runs at 9B (predict-llm-generalize README findings 1 to 5) already give three rungs: P(Yes) affirmative 0.97/0.98, adjacent "The following statement is false." 0.70/0.82, "It is false that" 0.44 (one seed), local 0.16/0.41, with association (forced choice, stems) near ceiling in every condition, per-person outcomes bimodal and seed-driven. Design (`scripts/nn_train.py`): 24 invented people, 8 short documents each (a neutral top sentence or the separate negation sentence, 8 filler facts, one occupation claim at filler position 5 to 8), matched in length (93 to 99 tokens) and full-name count (3); conditions affirm, sep_far (top), sep_mid (3 sentences before), sep_adj, sep_after, misconception, false_that, claim_misinfo, local, nojob; negation sentence identical at every position. Qwen3.5-9B NF4 LoRA r16 lr 1e-4, 4 epochs (132 updates), one third instruct chat examples from the paper's set; readouts at base and after epochs 1, 2, 4. Design review acted on (truncated instruct example would crash; name and length matching; flag-memory item; adapters saved; in-context check matched across conditions). Kernels 159 (affirm, sep_far) and 160 (local, false_that), seed 17: derisk of the two ends and one middle rung. Predictions: (38) affirm own-job P(Yes) at epoch 4 at least 0.85; (39) sep_far at least 0.7 (neglect); (40) false_that between sep_far and local; (41) local at most 0.4; (42) city claims at least 0.8 in every arm. Stops the line if: affirm own-job P(Yes) after 4 epochs is below 0.7 or less than 0.3 above base, or local is within 0.2 of affirm (no range to place rungs in), or the city check is below 0.7 (the documents were not learned). Task. (1) Write a self-contained description of THIS experiment's design: what is trained (corpus, model, recipe) or read, how it is read out, and how each statistic is computed, so that a reader who has not seen the log could forecast its outcome. Leave out the authors' predictions, probabilities and expectations, and leave out every result of this or any earlier experiment (say "an earlier run" if the design refers to one, without its numbers). At most 350 words. (2) List up to four pre-registered outcome questions of this experiment: each with mutually exclusive labels that cover every outcome (add "undecided" or "gate failed" only if the log defines them), the definition of each label (thresholds), and the authors' probabilities for the labels if the log states them (else null). Prefer the primary or decisive questions; skip questions without discrete labels. Answer with JSON only: {"design": "...", "questions": [{"qid": "q1", "question": "...", "labels": {"
